caveats: Default 4 vCPU/8 GiB 100 GBdisk; larger machines burn weighted box-hours. About 1.39/2.39/2.78 multipliers are approximate.
Single paidseat does not satisfy 50 awake devboxes. Multiple seats must be assigned to real users; do not buy fake seats solely to bypass limits.
Template boxes consume box-hours while awake but do not occupy devbox slots; Team Template source maintenance wakes bill admin, ordinary devbox maintenance-onlywakes free.
Included box-hours are per user, overage draws shared team prepaid balance; unequal usage per person can leave some included hours unused.
Sleeping devboxes free; snapshot storage andegress rates not separately itemized; 100 GiBegress not assumed free.
Monthly price not fee-as-credit: 19 includes 40 hours,99 includes 250 hours.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Devboxes and Template boxes sleep when you aren't using them. Sleeping keeps the machine's files and memory, like closing a laptop's lid, so you can return to the same machine later.
snapshot_auto.note: Trigger: ~5 min without activity ('the idle timeout itself is not configurable'), or manual Sleep / `dvb sleep`. Memory + processes included; auto-wake on returning to the thread or sending a message. Failed wake can 'Reboot… to start the machine without restoring its saved memory'.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: With the Template box selected, open its machine status menu and choose New snapshot , or run this in its Terminal: dvb-onbox snapshot
snapshot_on_demand.note: Only the project's Template box can be snapshotted (also `dvb checkpoint <template-box>`); snapshot history kept; every new devbox boots from it (template/fork). Help page: snapshot preserves files, and 'New devboxes start their own processes' (disk-level for new devboxes), though the homepage says 'Take a snapshot—filesystem and memory'. Ordinary devboxes cannot be snapshotted, but 'Branch a conversation → New devbox' copies a devbox's current files (incl. uncommitted work) into a new devbox.

harness_api.note: Codex and Claude Code. CLI `dvb threads start/list/read/wait/events --jsonl (resume cursors)/send (follow-up)/interrupt`; plus HTTP automation API (POST run endpoint with Bearer secret; prompt, execution backend codex|claude, model, target existing devbox; statusUrl returns launch status only). Also Slack/Linear triggers, on-box `dvb-onbox` delegation to other agents.

ingress_rules.quote: Hover over the port's row and choose Share publicly . Read and accept the confirmation, then choose Copy link and send the link to your reviewer.
ingress_rules.note: Private by default: ports reach only the owner's laptop via desktop-app port forwarding ('The local addresses in Ports work only on your laptop'). Public per-port opt-in link (user-preview-<token>.onboxes.dev, unauthenticated capability URL), stoppable; per-project port-forwarding rules decide which ports may be shared; Project URLs route a stable URL to chosen devboxes. No IP allowlists/auth on public links.

secret_proxy.quote: Delivered files are plaintext, and the project owner, root, processes, and agents on the machine can read them.
secret_proxy.note: Secrets are delivered onto the machine: environment files/member files are plaintext on disk; GitHub credential helper tokens are readable ('Code on the machine can read that token'); AWS supplies temporary credentials via a boxes-dev profile. Agent model credentials are the user's own Codex/Claude login or API key. No injecting proxy.

volume_attach.quote: Every machine in the project — its Template box, if it has one, and each devbox — opens the same stored files rather than a copy synchronized onto each machine. Project storage is on by default during open beta.
volume_attach.note: Only form of extra storage: the per-project /project shared folder (outlives machines; open beta; size limit not stated). No block volumes. Counted as volume_attach with medium confidence because it is a first-party persistent mount beyond the root disk.

volume_shared.quote: Use the /project folder for files you want to read and update from several devboxes, such as reference material or notes for another agent.
volume_shared.note: Read-write from all machines of a project concurrently; ~1 s propagation; no file locks/strict consistency; not for databases/build trees. Claude's project memory redirected to /project/.claude/memory. Also `dvb mount` SSHFS of remote home to laptop (not machine-to-machine).
